constraints: The contract must stay internally coherent: whenever plan steps or validation metrics imply tool access, requires_tools must be true and capability_lane must be "tool_required".

Explicit caller overrides must keep winning. If a payload supplies requires_tools, capability_lane, plan_steps, validation_metrics or review_checkpoints, that value must still be honoured over kind inference.
The finalized / reviewed flags and the terminal workflow stages (handoff, final, finalized, review_final) must keep forcing the tool lane; do not remove or reorder those short-circuits.
Keyword inference in normalize_task_kind must keep working unchanged, including the "coding" -> "code" alias and the general fallback.
Do not add new keys to the returned contract and do not change the values any existing key takes for kinds that are already coherent.
Prefer one owner for the kind sets over three independent literals that can drift apart again.
known_regression: The existing tests in auto-router do not catch this: tests/test_task_contract.py only exercises task_kind="coding", which IS in the requires_tools set and therefore passes, and task_kind="review" only together with finalized=True, which short-circuits before kind inference is reached. All nine affected kinds are untested. The lazy repair -- widening the set, or deleting the explicit-override short-circuit so kind inference always wins -- is caught by the broader acceptance tier, which pins override precedence, keyword inference and caller-supplied lists.
problem: auto_router/task_contract.py builds one contract per task: a task_kind, whether tools are required, a capability_lane, a workflow_stage, plan steps, validation metrics and review checkpoints. At this revision several of those fields contradict each other. A task whose kind is `refinement`, `repair`, `review`, `repo`, `patch`, `documentation`, `docs`, `terminal` or `shell` is handed the code-execution or operations plan -- including a step to make the smallest safe change, or apply the smallest safe operation -- and is handed validation metrics such as `regressions_checked`, `state_verified` or `change_applied`, while at the same time the same contract reports requires_tools=False and capability_lane="prompt_only" with workflow_stage="prompt_only". Downstream consumers read those fields: the routing path skips the tool lane entirely when requires_tools is false, and the job builder still grants terminal and code_execution toolsets. Repair the module so a contract never prescribes work that requires tool access while declaring that it does not require tool access.
title: build_task_contract emits self-contradictory contracts for nine task kinds
